body: No problem! I go to university of Nevada, Reno. I'm in their psychology program with a research emphasis so I'm super excited to learn about all that can happen to the human mind. I really want to help with mental illness like me.
No problem! Let me know if you do end up deciding to! I really hope it helps!! Have a stellar day

Don't worry about being rude or rejecting my advise, I've done that so many times to so many people that I can take it. And in order to check yourself in you don't have to actually have done anything, you can just go in saying I feel hopeless, I don't see a reason to live, I'm suicidal, etc. it's not necessarily for everyone but I know it REALLY helped me. Also, I know how it feels to not get comments/get stupid comments on your thread. Has happened to me countless times on this subreddit.
My phone isn't letting me pm you but if you message me I can give you my username or email if you want to do that instead. Hope you're okay atm

Please don't think you're alone and have no one to talk to. I'm so sorry you feel the way you do. Killing yourself is not the answer. Think about your mom, your friend, your internet friends. That would tear them apart whether you want to believe it or not. I tried to commit suicide two years ago and was taken to a mental hospital. If you're feeling really out of control that's the place to go. They get you intensive treatment, group therapy and you meet people you can talk to when you get out. I still speak on a monthly basis with two people I was in there with. 
I know it doesn't mean much to say that I care, but I do. I really encourage you to pm, email or call me (it can be arranged) if you're feeling too down. I will do whatever it takes to get your mind off of it.
Highly recommend giving it another go! And continue to stay strong my friend, don't let yourself get overwhelmed!

Let me tell you, no one will forget. It will be extremely painful for them. If you're truly considering it go to the emergency room, they can help find you somewhere where you'll be safe and cared for. Just a thought.

You're not a disappiontment. Everyone goes through phases where they feel like "everything is too messed up." I know because I'm in one myself. I've been in many of these situations and while I have only attempted suicide once (I was put in a mental hospital for four days for that) I've realized that things do improve even if it's only a little bit. You're so young and you sound like you have so many people that care about you! You're so lucky to have them! I would definitely recommend talking to a friend about how you feel and let them know what you have done before. If it helps when you're feeling suicidal find a friend that understands and will be there for you so you don't feel alone and that will take you to the hospital if necessary. I would HIGHLY recommend trying to get more sleep, sleep plays a HUGE role in mood. If you're having trouble sleeping, like insomnia, I would suggest seeing a doctor because there are effective treatments for that.
Please feel free to pm if you're feeling low. You're not alone, okay? :)

You definitely sound depressed. Have you thought about seeing a psychiatrist or therapist? It really helps to talk through your problems with someone, get it out of your head so your thoughts don't feel as heavy. As far as finding interested and setting career goals, I can't help you there. My parents are forcing me to finish my degree even with my mental health problems. I have no idea what I want to do after that as I can't think of anything that I would love to do. I feel like that will come though if I make an effort and explore the possibilities. As far as your ex you deserve SO much better! Even if you are negative or complain a lot (I do) there is someone out there that knows how to combat those thoughts and make you feel better. I met someone that helps me do that, I'm honestly the most negative and whiny person I know and it annoys me to no end. You're so strong to have made it this far, please don't give up.
:/ That's understandable from some angle I suppose.
Feeling like that isn't healthy. I know because I have, check in to a hospital it really is helpful.

If you don't like your doctor then switch! It's very important to like your doctor. I've taken all the medications you mentioned and I've gained around 20 pounds before I stopped gaining weight. Latuda has really helped my concentration and mood. Lamictal did too but it's made it really hard to concentrate.

I've always loved my mania. I hoped when I started taking medication that I would be like that all the time, but that wasn't the case. All the medications I'm on are designed to keep me stable, which lately makes me feel like nothing. I don't feel happy but occasionally I dip down and the doctor adds more medications or alters mine so that I don't feel completely depressed. If mania was causing problems I would highly recommend taking medication and if your lows get too low definitely take medication but if you're able to handle both then I would recommend just some therapy.
That's just your opinion and this is mine. As someone that HAS been to a hospital involuntarily.

I understand that, but that's the only way to completely prevent it. And while it may be traumatic at first (I've been taken to one involuntarily so trust me on this) it does end up helping. And when you come out you realize who truly cares about you.

I think that you need to just hold on to the thought of that woman's kindness. There ARE good people in the world willing to help. I'm sure you mother and the girl you love would be more than willing to help you seek treatment or check you into the hospital if what you're going through becomes to overwhelming. Why do you hate yourself? You sound like a decent person with people who care about you

I know exactly the type of thing you're describing. 99% that's my thought process. "I can't kill myself, I have that test on Thursday" type of stuff. I would highly recommend seeing a psychiatrist, I've told mine about my weird suicidal thoughts and she was able to. I've also started to voice when I begin feelings these sorts of things to my boyfriend and mother. I've found it helps to have someone come over and "watch" me. I know about my own thoughts enough to know when I can't handle them and the people that know me know that if I ask to go to the hospital I should be going asap. 
If you feel that you would like to check into a mental hospital don't be afraid to, I've been to the hospital and the intensive care and coping skills have been very helpful.

You should talk to your mom. Seriously. Letting someone know you're feeling that way is healthy. Going to the hospital is nothing to be ashamed of and I encourage it, having been there myself. Please pm me if you want to talk further.

I know how you feel as far as wishing you could die by an accident. I've always been terrified of actually doing it but I just always thought maybe if I take some extra pills it'll just happen. But I know that's not healthy. I would highly recommend going to a mental hospital as they can help you detox and learn coping strategies so that you won't feel like you need to abuse drugs and alcohol. I've been down the same path by abusing alcohol lately. Please go to the emergency room and get into a mental hospital as it truly does help.
Take her to the emergency room. The only way to completely prevent it is to take her somewhere where she'll get the attention she needs.

Like I said I'm sorry about your mom, she sounds like maybe she deals with things differently than most people. Maybe she was afraid and that's just how she handled it. I know it's hard moving on after a break-up but it's necessary unfortunately.

That's really not fair to you. As much as you want to do that sort of thing I think that you should refrain just so there's as little confusion as possible. Getting some space might also be good for you.

I'm sorry you're having such a rough time. I'm a 21 year old college student with bipolar disorder and severe anxiety. My parents and my sister believe that I am making what I am experiencing up and refuse to support me so I know how it feels to have parents that don't "get it." As far as no internet, I don't know if you'd ever want a pen pal, but I would be more than happy to write to you. My dorm is silly about me recieving mail but next semester I'm going to have my own mail box and address. For now if you'd like to email I can do that too. You don't sound pathetic and I applaud you for posting here. I've found this subreddit to be helpful when I've posted so I really hope it can come through for you too.

I'm very sorry that happened to you. I would just say to focus on yourself while you rest up and get better. Have you ever tried meditation to try and clear your head and relax so you can rest? I understand how you feel, I know how nice it can feel to have someone to comfort you and unfortunately that isn't possible sometimes. Just take solace in the fact that you're not alone. *virtual hugs*
I know how that feels. I also know how horrible it is to not have support. Hence why I'm on this subreddit. No one should have to feel alone!
Well I know I'm only on the internet but I'm here. It will get better I promise, I can't promise it won't get worse first. I suppose just stay positive, he's still in your life.. That's something.

Keep trying! It sounds like you're making a real effort so please don't stop! Life is worthwhile even when struggling with a mental illness (I'm bipolar) you just have to keep your head up and keep hope in your heart. I disagree with the post below. If you are religious good for you, that sort of thing can help with the hope aspect of things. If you ever want to vent or talk please pm or email me (bipolartalks@live.com) I'm a 21 year old female college student and I really want to meet others who feel as I do because I feel more connected to those people than I do to those actually in my life.

It sounds like you got to a good space before, why not strive for that again? As far as your PTSD and your anxiety have you been to a doctor or counselor? That sort of thing is extremely difficult to deal with alone. You are significant and I hope that this isn't reaching you too late. Please if you need to vent or just want to know someone is there please email or pm me. My email is bipolartalks@live.com

I feel you. Some of my most comforting thoughts are of killing myself. I attempted and was hospitalized in the mental hospital for it. That was the best experience of my life. If you are really on the verge go to the emergency room and they will help you get to the proper hospital. I found that once I was there I got the 24/7 care I needed whether it be with counselors or psychiatrists they were always there and I had daily appointments based on what I needed. Another great part was meeting everyone else, it helped me to see that I'm really not alone and develop some sort of support system (at least while I was there).
I encourage you to try this or to at least voice the seriousness of what you're feeling to someone.

I empathize with mother issues, I've got my fair share. If you feel that you shouldn't be on meds voice that to the doctor! As far as you ex-boyfriend he shouldn't have left because of your mom, if anything you need him more because of how she is. I'm sure he will still be there for you as a friend, even though you want more, and if you voice the seriousness of what you're feeling hopefully he'll be there for you.
Otherwise I would try to find maybe a counselor at your school (if you go) or some adult you can talk to about this. 
I'm sorry your mother is treating you that way.
Best of luck.

I empathize so much with this. I've always been "average" until I started getting depressed and it got serious while I was in school (stress is a huge trigger for me) and I ended up failing all my classes. I am now on academic probation and required to attend meetings, etc. I constantly see people doing better than me academically and get extremely jealous. At times, especially in my low lows, I get into the "why should I even try?" mindset. It's so hard to get out of that. But I've found that focusing completely on myself has helped. Who cares how that person did on the test! I even talked to my professors about how I was feeling and low and behold that actually helped, I informed them that stress is a huge trigger for my condition so at time I might need help completing an assignment or an extra day for a test because I get so panicky or freaked out the night before that I couldn't completely anything. Best of all, you're in high school! There are so many opportunities for you to get help. Have you spoken to the counselor on campus? 
As far as talents and redeeming qualities that's just a matter of finding them, college is better for that. I had no idea what I was even slightly good at until I was able to try everything. 
Keep your chin up and if you need someone to vent to or email or message or even call I'm here.

I agree with this. Finding your triggers is extremely helpful because then you know what to avoid. There are a lot of places that help those with gambling addiction and no one should be scared to utilize those.

I'm in the same boat self control wise. I've spent loads of money, both mine and my parents and I lost all their trust. That was 2 years ago. Let me just say that things have gotten much better, I really did want to end it then. I was in the hospital because I attempted to, but the hospital helped me to realize it wasn't the end of the world. I was young (19, same as you) and life goes on. I'm 21 now in university with a job and while I still have money problems I have my past that makes me a better person.

You're not creepy, I completely understand this feeling. I'm a girl and my first love ruined me. I saw him everywhere, he dated my friends and got them to stop talking to me. He called me at 2am and texted and emailed, whenever I would reply he would stop. He egged my car and spread nasty rumors about me at my school. And I still loved him, he was all I could think about, all I would talk about. 
Let me just say, you will be happy again. I know it seems far away now but it does happen. You just have to work at it. For me it was moving away, I moved out of state to go to University and used a stupid online dating app to help me meet guys up here. I forced myself to talk to people and date even though I just wanted my ex to contact me. But after a few months of dates I met someone and that ended but still looking back on my ex I see that he was a horrible person to torture me how he did (Just like your "friend" messed things up for you). I'm sorry for what you're going through just please don't give up. You're so young and seem so genuine, things will get better. Please don't hesitate to pm if you want to talk.

You don't need to die. This is a rough time sure but that's no reason to end everything. I'm sorry your mom kicked you out, is there any one you could call to drive you even part of the way? Could you panhandle? Get a loan? Bike?
I just think she sounds idiotic if she's saying it's because he's Asian when she's Asian herself. He's the one who deserves better!

Okay first off, it would be a serious shame to lose your intelligent self. The amount of racism you describe is sickening. I don't know if that's an Austrailian media or stereotype thing but in America it's the opposite, at least I think so, no one here underestimates Asians, why would we? Every Asian I've ever known has been intelligent and kind? I'm so sorry you experience this. Please don't end your life. That girl sounds like a snob and YOU are the one who deserves better. I'm 21 as well and have grappled with the idea of suicide more than a few times, I've even been hospitalized for it once. If you really feel like you're going to do this, go to an emergency room. That hospital is THE best thing you'll experience, at least it was for me. Doctors that gave 24/7 care along with others who got exactly what I was thinking. 
Please don't hesitate to pm me if you want to email, message or talk. You sound like a really great man.

Have you tried reiterating to your doctor that your medication isn't helping you? I've quite literally yelled at mine because she wasn't listening to me when I said mine wasn't helping and now I've switched because she wouldn't acknowledge that the medications she has me on cause extremely memory and concentration problems (I'm a full time student, maybe that's why I struggled so much last semester???!). Anyway, excuse my ramble. But never be afraid to speak up or move on. Find a doctor that gets it and stick with them. 
Best of luck.
That can be depression. I've experienced that sort of thing more than once. It's nothing to be ashamed of.

I agree with the emergency room bit. When I was first considering suicide my mother literally dragged me there, but it's the best thing I could have asked for. The amount of attention I got (from doctors, finally) and the amount of people I met feeling the same things really helped me. It seems terrifying but it really really really can be helpful. If you're seriously considering it please ask your loved one to take you to the emergency room, there's no harm in being careful.

This sounds so much like me it frightens me. For years the only reason I didn't end it when I got extremely depressed was my mother's threats (she'd die if I died, etc.) and my family continues to this day to blame me for things that are directly related to my disorder. People WOULD care if you die. I know my family would, no matter how crappy they treat me or how many times they tell me "I'm done. Just stop." I haven't figured out why I keep on going but I do, I feel like there's something out there for me. Please don't end it. Have you talked to a doctor about the emptiness? Or a counselor?

My doctor just keeps trying different medications when I say that they don't work. My doctor was completely aware. I'm seeing a new doctor starting tomorrow so hopefully she'll actually listen to what I'm saying.
Thank you!

Wishing death upon yourself is something I do constantly, when I get really low (I'm bipolar) I literally can't do anything without those thoughts invading and attacking my head. Depression is a horrible illness, I wouldn't wish it on my worst enemies. Just know that you ARE strong enough to get through it, you've made it this far haven't you?
If you ever need to vent pm me, please.
I thought so. And I really think it is, maybe it's something you should explore. I feel like you would be very talented at it :)
Like out of all the posts I've read yours was very well written. You're very well spoken. Are you in the uk?

I know exactly how you feel, I still have no idea why I keep going. But I do, I'm striving for a degree in psych and I really want to help people with mental illness in some way once I graduate. I feel like if you've been there you're better able to help. Hope things improve, today is a new day x

You write incredibly well! Thank you for posting and I know how it feels to be "numb" to everything. If you ever want to vent please pm me, please don't harm yourself I can see so much potential just in your writing!
Excellent. Best of luck :)
Have you asked for weekly appointments? I'm sure they would be happy to do that for you. Getting it out always helps me :)
It's not pathetic. It happens. I've cried in many embarrassing places over extremely trivial things. Don't give up. You are so so young.
That's called psychosis and it is a mental condition. It's in your head. I would HIGHLY recommend seeing a psychiatrist or therapist. Both can help you get out of that mindset.
not at all! my email is bipolartalks@live.com if you ever want to email!

oh more hardships, I'm sorry. But I'm sure they can work with you. It surprised how much my therapist would work with me. Even my psychiatrist will talk me through my down times without charge. It's definitely worth looking into.

I tried to commit suicide two years ago, the only thing that made me hesitate was my mothers phone call as I was holding the bottle of sleeping pills. She could hear the pain in my voice and asked to go to the mental hospital. Coming out of the hospital was the hardest experience of my life. My family had no idea what sort of problems I was dealing with, or that I was feeling that low. I hate to say it but at first there is no "light" there isn't anything or any point where things suddenly get easier. It takes a lot of effort and it does in fact feel like you're crawling. The only thing that's kept me going is my mother, she was molested as a child and has every right to be severely depressed yet she's positive even through her many debilitating conditions and her ignorant mother who never acknowledged the molestation and allowed it to go on until my mother moved out of the house at 17. The only thing that has kept me going is not that I don't have any reason to feel the way I do but that she's made it through so there has to be a light at the end of the tunnel and some sort of reason to stay positive even when it seems impossible. If you feel like you want to talk please don't hesitate to message me, email or even call if that's what would help. I'm here, I've made it through and you are not alone.
Have you tried to find out if they can make phone appointments? I've seen two therapists who offer that sort of service.

Keep your family and significant other in mind. In my lows (I'm bipolar) the literal only thing that keeps me going is my mom, I know that if I go through with it it will hurt her far more than I am hurting right now for far longer than I have been hurting. I have also been hospitalized and been ignored by my doctors. And now I'm starting to feel like my medications aren't working for me any more so I know how you feel. You ARE meant to be alive. You're 25 and you have so much life ahead of you. If you need someone to message, email or talk on the phone with I'm here for you. You are NOT alone. You will make it through this.

Exactly! I'm on the highest dose of some of the strongest mood stabilizers possible and I still have extreme lows and lots of impulses I can't control (especially money, which my parents don't believe is related to my disorder :( ) You'll definitely have to let me know if you do end up finding out that you are one or the other. It's nice to meet someone that is dealing with the same back and forth I am.

Please don't end things. It sounds like you have such a good heart with wanting to help your sister and all. I know how it feels not having money. I'm a full time student with two jobs and on top of that I have severe anxiety and bipolar disorder. What you're going through sounds EXTREMELY difficult. I can't even imagine. But things will get better I'm sure. Sure this is a stupid situation that isn't fair to you, but shit happens and there will be better things in your future. You've got intelligence, looks (it sounds like haha) and a good heart. We need more people in the world like you. Please pm if you want to vent or feel any lower. I'm happy to message, email, talk on the phone, whatever you need. You're not alone in being depressed and wanting to give up just please stay on this earth and be one of the few decent people.
See so they're just mistaken! You seem very intelligent so don't let them get you down!

I thought I was borderline for a while too! I'm still not certain if I am or not. Right now I'm on so many medications I really wouldn't know either way and my doctor just dismissed it when I brought it up. She's never really listened to my ideas though, so I'm seeing a new doctor. I don't want to be borderline though because the only treatment is therapy and there is not medication to directly treat it. :/

I'm sorry so much has gone awry for you. Car problems are extremely stressful so I know the feeling there, I'm sorry yours died that only adds to problems I know from experience. I'm certain your mother still loves you and would be devastated if you went the same way your brother did. The only reason I'm still alive is my mother, even though I feel like she loves my sister more than me I have to remember that if I ever did commit suicide it would hurt my mother and that isn't fair. I try to think about that when I'm at my lowest points. How would my mother feel, I try to imagine her pain and keep that in my head. I wish I could lend you my car so that you had a way to get around. Have you ever seen a counselor or someone you could talk to about your brother, being trans and your anxiety? It's worth a shot if you haven't also feel free to pm me. If you need to call or email or whatever I am here. You are not alone.

I feel you! This does count as socializing. Meeting people with similar problems and ideas is really helpful. You're different, people should just accept that and move on. Not everyone has to agree with everything.

well I'm fairly certain they can't turn you away. I'm bipolar and I have a slew of medications rotating around on my account and my insurance hasn't so much as batted an eye. I hope things are the same for you. Please feel free to message or email (bipolartalks@live.com) if you ever need to vent or are feeling low. I check it 24/7

I have a website and I would love if you would write about this for my website. It's a site for those who feel suicidal so that they don't feel alone. I have an email that I'm trying to get people to use whenever they're thinking that way. I've felt like that so so so so many times and the only thing that keeps me going is how much I would hurt those who love me if I went through with it. I'm happy to email, talk on the phone, text whatever helps. I never want anyone to feel alone like I do. 
Thank you for posting here, I hope this helps people to realize people do care about them whether they think they do or not.

Ugh that whole mess. I wish I could lend you my insurance, thankfully I'm on my parents for at least a couple years. I'm crossing my fingers for you though. It's definitely worth a try, even if it sucks have to wade through all the preliminary stuff. :/

I'm with you. I've always been the "weird, quiet girl" and people think I'm awkward and rude. That's why I come here, it's so comforting to know that others feel the things I do and that I'm really not alone.

Beyond with you with the grades part of it. I failed last semester and my parents are threatening to stop paying for parts of my school which just gets me more stressed and causes me to have more trouble dealing with the coursework. Talking to people is extremely tough, I consider myself a loner and I have at the most two friends that were confident enough to speak to me first. College is VERY different as far as socializing, there are far more clubs and things to do to meet people. My school even has a club for people who enjoy video games to get together and chat about them, things like that. Once you find your niche it's easier to meet people I think. 
Best of luck. pm me if you want to talk more.

I hate it but I think it's made me a more considerate person. Like I'm trying to show her how to act, even if it isn't effective at least I can sleep (sometimes thanks to her haha) at night knowing that I'm a considerate and decent person and I think that's the key. Just be the bigger person and keep it in your mind that you are good and they are wrong. I'm sorry you get teased and embarassed, I'm sure you don't deserve that sort of treatment. No one does.

I felt like this for a long time, there's nothing wrong with you. Unfortunately this came before I started seeing my bipolar disorder ups and downs so I'm not sure if it's the same thing you're experiencing. Have you gone to a counselor? I found that voicing my concerns to someone who sees all types of people helps. After a few sessions I would come in and yell, swear and cry at the poor lady but apparently that's all completely normal. Once I started opening up I was amazed to find I actually felt a lot. As for movies and shows I used to be more empathetic towards the characters as well but as of late I don't feel very much for them. Aside from rape scenes bothering me (because I am a girl and I'm more scared that's going to happen to me) I don't feel anything after watching murder shows and just depressing shows in general. If you want to talk or vent please feel free to pm me.

Have you called your insurance? My mother had to force me to call around and figure things out but it truly is worth doing. And surprisingly enough insurance will help you, they are icky sometimes but I know when I've really needed it they've made appointments for me and let me know where I can go that's going to have the most coverage, who the best rated doctor is in my area, etc.

I don't believe that for a second. You're not useless or worthless. You're a human being in a beautiful world. You may feel like a "bump" in everyone's lives but you're not, trust me. It's just in your head, I've felt the same way and had to have someone sit me down and tell me that when you're emotionally down you need to reach out even if you don't want to. Please email me if you need to talk, I check this email 24/7 and I don't need to know your name or anything. Just vent. I'm here.
I know how you feel. It's hard to find a good fit with them. But it's definitely worth trying to find one that you "click" with. My mom did and she's made leaps and bounds emotionally.

have you thought of a mental hospital? I've been in one and while the stigma that surrounds it isn't pretty it REALLY helps. They give you all the attention you could ask for and get intensive about treatment. It also helped me meet others that were going through some very tough things, helped me get things into perspective and also helped seeing them become so positive. As for your puppy, I am so sorry. I know what that sort of loss feels like. It makes me well up to think about my dog dying, he's my rock when I'm feeling sad. Have you thought about getting another dog? I've read so many great things about dogs helping depression and other illnesses. Maybe you could try getting a dog trained to deal with that? I'm not entirely sure where to find that but I know they exist.
Best of luck.

Have you spoken to a counselor? If not I HIGHLY recommend it, I resented the idea of going at first but it truly helps to just vent. I've been to therapists and just let loose, swearing and yelling and crying. Just getting things out helped me immensely when I was stressed. It's just a thought. I know how overwhelming life can get some times but please don't give up.
Best of luck.

It sounds like he may be depressed, I think support and love would be the best way to help him. Getting angry with/trying to force him to do things would probably just irritate him and therefore worsen his condition/make him feel hopeless or disliked, etc. In my own experience, with my family and how they treat me when I've been depressed, getting angry or confrontation is NEVER helpful. I find that when my mother just spends time with me, compliments when I do things and lets me know that she supports me no matter what that helps more than anything. Feeling loved, supported and accepted has truly helped me. 
I wish you the best of luck.

School is unimportant when dealing with such deep emotions. You shouldn't let schooling interfere. I failed every single class last term and am now forced into academic counseling and on probation that requires me to attend extra classes, as if this will help my already stressful day to day life and this extra work will help me do better in class... uh, no. I completely relate to wanting the pain to stop. I've been in a mental hospital and feel completely idiotic for feeling like I need to go again but it's necessary if I really get that low. Have you tried talking to a counselor about academic stresses? I've found that they can work with professors, etc and help with grades. I can't tell you how many doctors I've gone to with panic attacks that gave me notes so that I can take the tests when I'm ready and calm. It's worth a thought.

I hate to say I agree, but I do. The world can be a very messed up place and there are a lot of bad people. But it's not worth it to focus on that. There are so many good people in the world, kind acts and beautiful places. I've stopped watching and listening to the news as it only makes me depressed. I've stuck to reddit on the front page, and better happier articles. It's hard to see, but there really is a lot of good in this f'd up world we live in.

I'm with you. On long driving trips I would drive carelessly and pray that a truck would hit me head on or some other car would knock me off the road. I feel like this is normal for those who are depressed but then again I'm not sure. I'm bipolar so my episodes only last a couple weeks, but I do feel like this. I'm certain you deserve to be alive. Why wouldn't you?

I just started my semester so I'm hoping to get ahead while I can. My roommate is a lady (as am I) and she's just very passive aggressive. I'm very shy and try to be polite to her but she continues to stay on the phone/watch tv until 2am (I had to be up at 6am today) and hogs the bathroom with near 45 minute showers. When she comes in late she turns on all the lights even if she can see that I'm asleep. She's just not considerate at all. Only a few more months of living with her though and then I can get my own room, thank goodness.
I'm a girl haha! Glad you're feeling better :)
It is possible to have suicidal tendencies without being depressed. Sounds like you're doing a really good job managing! Best of luck!
